description: This topic covers specific technical terms used in various sports. It is frequently tested in the Static GK section of competitive exams, often as direct matching questions or identifying the sport associated with a given term.

sections.title: Important Terminologies of Cricket
sections.description: Highly tested technical terms and fielding positions associated with the game of Cricket.

key_associations.extra_info: A fielding position placed unusually and dangerously close to the batsman on the off side.
A method of dismissal where the ball would have hit the stumps but is obstructed by the batsman's leg or pad.
A deceptive delivery bowled by a leg-spinner that spins inwards towards a right-handed batsman instead of spinning away.
An over bowled in which no runs are scored by the batsmen.
A delivery bowled such that it pitches right at or very close to the batsman's toes/feet.

sections.title: Terminologies of Football and Hockey
sections.description: Crucial terms from Football and Hockey that often confuse students in multiple-choice questions.

key_associations.extra_info: A method used to restart play after it has been stopped for an injury or non-penalty reason.
Also known as a 'Short Corner', awarded to the attacking team for a foul committed by defenders inside the striking circle.
A rule violation that occurs when an attacking player is closer to the opponent's goal line than both the ball and the second-last opponent.
The act of moving the ball forward while maintaining control and maneuvering past opponents.
Achieving three consecutive successes, such as scoring three goals in a match or taking three consecutive wickets.

sections.title: Terminologies of Tennis and Badminton
sections.description: Important terms related to racquet sports, especially regarding scoring systems and shots.

key_associations.extra_info: A powerful, aggressive overhead shot that is hit downward with force, making it difficult to return.
A tied score (e.g., 40-40 in tennis) where a player must win two consecutive points to win the game.
A term used universally in racquet sports to represent a score of zero (e.g., '15-Love').
Called when a served ball touches the net but still lands in the correct service box; the serve is replayed without penalty.
Making two consecutive illegal or failed serves, which results in the loss of a point.

sections.title: Boxing, Chess and Other Sports
sections.description: Key terminologies of combat sports, board games, and popular American sports.

key_associations.extra_info: A winning condition when a boxer is knocked down and is unable to stand up before the referee counts to 10.
A powerful, upward punch thrown aimed at the opponent's chin.
The final game-winning position where the opponent's king is under attack and has no legal move to escape.
An opening chess move in which a player sacrifices a pawn or minor piece to gain a strategic positional advantage.
A hit that allows the batter to successfully touch all the bases and score a run on the same play.
A grappling hold in which a wrestler passes their arm under the opponent's arm and behind their neck.

sections.title: Major Sports and Names of their Playing Areas
sections.description: Specific terminology used for the venues or playing areas of various sports, frequently asked as matching questions.

key_associations.extra_info: The specifically shaped playing field for baseball, forming a diamond shape.
An oval-shaped, banked track specifically built for track cycling events.
The enclosed, square platform where boxing bouts or skating events take place.
The designated enclosed area for horse riding and equestrian sports.
The main playing surface; in cricket, it refers specifically to the 22-yard strip in the center.
